data.offer: Loadline is a transportation management system for regional carriers: dispatch, a driver app, billing and customer tracking in one place.
data.title: 12 checks before you switch freight software
data.intro: For the operations and dispatch leads at Kestrel Freight Lines who will own the move off the 2016 system. It covers the data you keep, the connections you need, the people who sign off, and the first weeks after the switch.

checks.title: Export a full year of loads, rates and invoices from the current system
checks.why: Once the old contract ends, the history behind every rate dispute and audit goes with it.

checks.title: List every spreadsheet dispatch uses alongside the system
checks.why: Each one is a step the new setup has to cover, or it comes back within a month.

checks.title: Write down how a load moves from order to invoice today, step by step
checks.why: A vendor can only match a process you can describe, and the gaps show up here first.

checks.title: Ask the top ten customers how they want status updates
checks.why: Tracking links, EDI and emailed updates are set up differently, and changing later means a second rollout.

checks.title: Confirm which customers and brokers need EDI or API connections
checks.why: A missing connection on day one means loads keyed in by hand on both sides.

checks.title: Check the ELD and fuel card providers have a supported connection
checks.why: Without it, hours of service and fuel data have to be entered again for every driver.

checks.title: Define a clean customer and lane record before the import
checks.why: Duplicate customers and lanes imported as they are stay messy in the new system for years.

checks.title: Name one owner each for dispatch, billing and driver setup
checks.why: When nobody owns a piece, it is the piece that is still half done at go-live.

checks.title: Run two weeks of live loads in the new system alongside the old one
checks.why: Parallel running is the only way to find a billing gap before a customer does.

checks.title: Train drivers on the new app before the switch, not after
checks.why: A driver who meets the app for the first time at a loading dock calls dispatch instead.

checks.title: Agree the cutover date with billing, not just dispatch
checks.why: A switch mid-cycle leaves invoices split across two systems at month end.

checks.title: Keep read access to the old system for at least six months
checks.why: Audits, claims and rate questions keep coming after the switch, and they reference old loads.

data.closing: If any of these is still open at Kestrel, reply to my email with the one you are least sure about and I will send what I know on it.
